ca_warm_up_boulder_6.blurb: Warm-up Boulder is one boulder on the east side of Holcomb Valley, in the mountains above Big Bear Lake. It holds eight problems, and nearly all sit at the bottom of the scale: six are at the easiest level of bouldering and two are around V1. That suits a first few minutes of movement before heading to harder rocks in the same part of the valley, and it works for newer climbers too. The boulder is the first one met after passing through the gap in the fence line, roughly a minute's stroll in, and it takes a lot of sun. Landings across this stretch of the valley are mostly flat.

ca_the_happy_turtle.blurb: The Happy Turtle is a compact outcrop in the Campsite 7 area of Keller Peak, in the San Bernardino Mountains above Running Springs. It has eight bouldering problems, all at gentle grades: two at the easiest level, three around V0 and three around V1. Landings are mostly flat, and a straightforward downclimb on one side of the rock means no one needs to jump. It sits a short scramble up the slope from the roadside Asphalt Boulder, close to Arborescence Slab, so it combines easily with the other boulders nearby. Good for beginners and for anyone building up a circuit of low-grade problems at about 6,700 feet.

ca_writer_s_block_sheephead_mountain.blurb: Writer's Block is a twin-spire formation right beside Interstate 8 in south San Diego County, reached by a short drive off the freeway and an approach of about ten minutes. It has eight lines across four styles: three sport routes, two top-rope lines, two trad routes and one boulder problem. Grades start around 5.5 and 5.6 on the gentler trad and sport lines, climb through 5.8 to low 5.10 on the top-rope and sport lines, and finish with an unfinished 5.13 project. The rock is heavily featured. The spire's north face stays shaded all day, which makes it a cool option when the sun is strong, and the two top-rope lines are on that face.

ca_stack_1.blurb: Stack 1 is the most prominent block in the Little Free Library, a roadside bouldering spot on Keller Peak in the San Bernardino Mountains. It has eight problems that wrap around three of its sides, ranging from the easiest grade up to V3: three are at the lowest level, one is V0, one V1, two V2 and one V3. The block sits right beside Book Return Boulder, with a walk in of a minute or less from the road. The whole Library is made of boulders stacked like books on a shelf, with textured stone, and it gives low-grade climbers plenty to work on alongside a few harder problems.

ca_pachyderm_wall_aka_sunshine_wall.blurb: Pachyderm Wall, also called Sunshine Wall, is a wall at the Burney crag near Redding, about 26 miles east along Highway 299. The wall stands roughly 30 to 35 metres high and has the crag's longest lines. It is a mix of sport, trad, top-rope and aid routes: four sport lines around 5.10, one at 5.11 and one at 5.12, plus two aid routes at the easiest aid grade. It faces south and receives sun all day, so summers in Redding are too hot for it; autumn, winter and spring are the better seasons, and on cool days an early start helps. The trail from the highway is steep and turns slick after heavy rain.

ca_sunny_side.blurb: Sunny Side is one of the two walls of the Geological Time Corridor in the Split Rocks section of Joshua Tree National Park's Pinto Basin, at about 4,300 feet. It has eight routes, split evenly between top rope and traditional protection, with grades running from 5.5 up to a single 5.11. Most lines are slab and face climbs rather than cracks, so the character is different from the splitter crack climbing found elsewhere in the corridor. The wall sees full sun for most of the day. To reach it, follow the corridor approach and take the sunny branch rather than the shady one.

ca_the_bakery.blurb: The Bakery is a small clump of rock in the Iceberg Boulder Area of Rattlesnake Canyon, Indian Cove, in Joshua Tree National Park. It lies between the parking area and the Boortemus formation, and is reached by the same walk used for Finley's Rock. Eight routes are here: six trad, one sport and one top rope. Grades run from 5.3 to 5.11, though most fall at 5.9 and 5.10. The area was developed recently and has little fixed gear, so expect to lead on your own protection. Several hard trad lines have still to be climbed.

ca_wave_boulder_6.blurb: Wave Boulder is one of the boulders in the Puppy Boulders, a cluster beside the river in Tuolumne Meadows, Yosemite National Park, at about 8,500 feet. It has eight problems, mostly at low grades: one at the easiest level, three around V0, two around V1 and two at V2. The side facing the river has the gentler problems, while the uphill side offers a couple of more fingery ones. The stretch beside the water draws a crowd, so bring pads and a few friends. The Puppy Boulders are a short walk from the wilderness office parking lot, passing the bear lockers.

_conflicts.ca_pachyderm_wall_aka_sunshine_wall: Stored rock is siltstone but both fetched pages (https://www.mountainproject.com/v/109039768 and https://www.mountainproject.com/area/107305069/burney-limestone-aka-the-shredding) call the rock limestone; left unchanged and no rock word used in the blurb.
